research_rationale: Read the whole order (38 FR 2207, signed 1973-01-19; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11698.txt): a recital that the Convention on the Taking of Evidence Abroad in Civil or Commercial Matters was proclaimed on September 15, 1972 and came into force on October 7, 1972, and one operative sentence designating the Department of Justice as the Central Authority to receive Letters of Request coming from a judicial authority of another Contracting State and to transmit them to the authority competent to execute them. The order states no duration, date or condition that ends the designation. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes: current-law:usc (release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09) has 0 hits for this order; current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14) has 0 hits; later-events:ofr_catalog has 0 hits, so the Office of the Federal Register disposition notes record no amendment, revocation or supersession. The only other held text that names the order is the 1989 codification snapshot (ofr-codification-1989), which prints a SOURCE line citing it for a Title 28 provision; as a 1989 snapshot it shows history, not current force, and is not relied on as a current basis. Limitations disclosed: the order cites no authority statute (only the President's authority as President), and the packet holds no text of the Convention or of any withdrawal from it, so continuation rests on the held original plus the bounded searches finding no later instrument.
savings_reason: The order has no saving clause and no transitional provision. It issues one designation and revokes or amends nothing. The three bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes) found no pending-matter residue or later instrument, so the state is none after bounded search.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end. The order's own text (38 FR 2207) states no date, duration or condition that ends the designation. The later-events:ofr_catalog search has 0 hits and the held-corpus search for its number finds only the order's own printing and the 1989 codification SOURCE line; none revokes, supersedes or amends it.
scope_check: The order has one operative command: the Department of Justice is designated as the Central Authority to receive Letters of Request from a judicial authority of another Contracting State and to transmit them to the competent authority. The preamble recital about the Convention (proclaimed September 15, 1972; in force October 7, 1972) and Article 2 is background, not a separate command, so the inventory is one clause covering the whole text.
independent_command_check: There is no independent one-time command: the sole sentence is a standing designation, not a deadline, performance or revocation, so no clause can be exhausted by performance. No other command in the order survives or ends separately.
savings_check: No saving clause or transitional provision appears in the order, and it revokes or amends no earlier instrument, so there is no preserved right, pending matter or earlier instrument to carry forward. The three bounded searches found no residue.

The order has no own-terms end. research_rationale: Read the whole order (31 FR 10603, signed 1966-08-05; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11295.txt): under 3 U.S.C. 301 and the President's authority, section 1 designates and empowers the Secretary of State to exercise, without further presidential action, the authority conferred on the President by the first section of the Act of July 3, 1926 (22 U.S.C. 211a) to designate and prescribe rules governing the granting, issuing and verifying of passports; section 2 supersedes Executive Order 7856 of March 31, 1938 and Executive Order 8820 of July 11, 1941, subject to section 3; section 3 saves the rules and regulations in those orders, and those issued under them, in force when the order was issued until revoked or amended in pursuance of the authority conferred by this order, unless sooner terminated by operation of law. The dossier inventory omitted the recital and section 1, so it is corrected with inventory overrides (five clauses covering the whole text). The order has no own-terms end. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes. later-events:ofr_catalog has 2 hits: the Office of the Federal Register note 'Provisionally supersedes: EO 7856, EO 8820' (the order's own effect on earlier orders) and a see-reference to 55 FR 3676 and Executive Order 14348 (September 5, 2025). The held text of Executive Order 14348 (90 FR 43895) mentions this order only as one basis for geographic passport restrictions in its section 3(d); it does not amend, revoke or supersede it. current-law:usc has 3 hits: the 22 U.S.C. 211a note prints the order with no ending statement. current-law:ecfr has 3 hits: 22 CFR parts 22 and 51 cite the order in their authority lines. The authority statutes are checked: 3 U.S.C. 301 (held, jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t3-s301.txt) and 22 U.S.C. 211a (held) are both in the U.S. Code and still authorize the delegation. The held-corpus search for the number 11295 found no revocation or supersession.
savings_reason: Section 3 saves the rules and regulations contained in the superseded Executive Orders 7856 and 8820 and those issued under them that were in force on 1966-08-05, continuing until revoked or amended under the authority conferred by this order unless terminated by operation of law. The held current regulations (22 CFR parts 22 and 51) cite this order as authority, so the passport rule-making continues under section 1; no held source shows a particular saved rule still in force or ended, so the saved rules are treated as continuing under section 3 and as carried into the Department of State regulations.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end of section 1 or section 3. The order states no date, duration or condition ending them; the three bounded searches show no amendment, revocation or supersession (Executive Order 14348 only cites the order); 22 CFR parts 22 and 51 and the U.S. Code note still cite it. The supersession of Executive Orders 7856 and 8820 in section 2 is a one-time command, complete on issuance (1966-08-05).
scope_check: Five clauses after correction: the authority recital and section 1 (delegation of passport rule-making authority), the introductory line of section 2, section 2(1) (supersession of Executive Order 7856), section 2(2) (supersession of Executive Order 8820) and section 3 (saving provisions). Together they cover the whole text; the dossier's four clauses missed section 1.
independent_command_check: The supersession of Executive Orders 7856 and 8820 in section 2 is an independent one-time command, performed on issuance, and is recorded as terminated on 1966-08-05 by its own terms, not by any later instrument; it does not affect the continuing delegation in section 1, and section 3 separately keeps the rules of the superseded orders alive. Section 1 and section 3 are continuing.
savings_check: Section 3 is the order's saving clause. It keeps the rules and regulations contained in the superseded orders and issued under them, in force on 1966-08-05, in full force and effect until revoked or amended in pursuance of this order's authority. No held source identifies a specific saved rule that survives or ended, which is disclosed; the continuing current regulations in 22 CFR parts 22 and 51 cite this order as authority.

research_rationale: Read the whole order (24 FR 5233, signed 1959-06-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10826.txt): section 1 lets the Civil Service Commission confer a benefit under an Executive order on a Federal employee or former employee who met its requirements but became ineligible solely because an agency erred or overlooked making a timely determination or recommendation, only after the agency makes the required determination, with no action effective before the date it is taken; section 2 denies appeal rights against personnel actions made effective before the agency is notified of the grant; section 3 revokes Executive Order 10535 of June 9, 1954. The order has no own-terms end. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes. later-events:ofr_catalog has 1 hit, the Office of the Federal Register note 'Amended by: EO 12107, December 28, 1978'; the held text of Executive Order 12107 (44 FR 1055, signed 1978-12-28) section 2-101 amends and revises each listed order, among them 10826, by substituting the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission, and section 2-404 makes the order effective January 1, 1979, so the amendment is recorded as a later event and does not end the order. current-law:usc has 0 hits (no U.S. Code note names the order). current-law:ecfr has 3 hits: 5 CFR 351.501 and 5 CFR 351.502, whose eCFR text (351.502 in effect on 2026-09-02) still refers to cases under Executive Order 10826 to correct certain administrative errors, pending resolution by OPM. The authority the order cites, section 2 of the Civil Service Act and Revised Statutes 1753 (5 U.S.C. 631), is the derivation of 5 U.S.C. 3301 (Pub. L. 89-554, 1966), held at jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t5-s3301.txt, which still authorizes the President to prescribe regulations for admission into the civil service and was amended by Pub. L. 119-60 on December 18, 2025. The held-corpus search for the order's number found no revocation or supersession.
savings_reason: The order has no saving clause. Section 3 revoked Executive Order 10535 on issuance and no held source restores it. Section 2 limits only appeal rights in cases where a grant is made, which is part of the continuing grant of authority. The three bounded searches found no other residue or later instrument.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end. The order states no date, duration or condition ending section 1 or 2. The only amending instrument found, Executive Order 12107 (effective 1979-01-01), substitutes the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission and keeps the order; the held-corpus search for the number 10826 found no revocation or supersession, and current 5 CFR 351.502 still refers to cases under the order.
scope_check: One clause covers the whole text: section 1 (authority to confer a benefit in specified agency-error cases, with its proviso), section 2 (no appeal right from earlier-effective personnel actions) and section 3 (revocation of Executive Order 10535). The inventory span (characters 704-2278) covers all three sections. Executive Order 12107's substitution of the Office of Personnel Management is an amendment of the same clause, not a separate command.
independent_command_check: Section 3, the revocation of Executive Order 10535 of June 9, 1954, is a one-time command completed on issuance (1959-06-25); it needs no further performance and does not affect the continuing authority in section 1. Section 2 attaches to a grant under section 1 and continues with it.
savings_check: No saving clause appears in the order. Revocation of Executive Order 10535 is complete and no held source restores it; the three bounded searches found no other preserved right or pending matter needing separate treatment.

research_rationale: Read the whole order (18 FR 2069, signed 1953-04-10; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10444.txt): it further amends Executive Order 8809 of June 28, 1941 (Good Conduct Medal), as amended by Executive Order 9323 of March 31, 1943, to read as a single restated paragraph, issued under the President's authority as President and Commander in Chief (no authority statute is cited). The restated text establishes the Good Conduct Medal for exemplary behavior, efficiency and fidelity under regulations the Secretary of the Army and the Secretary of the Air Force prescribe, for enlisted men of the Army and Air Force who on or after August 27, 1940 completed three years of active Federal military service, or served one year after December 7, 1941 while the United States is at war, or at the end of service had completed less than three years if any part was after June 27, 1950, with a proviso that no one except persons separated for physical disability incurred in line of duty receives it for under one year. The order has no own-terms end. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes. later-events:ofr_catalog has 1 hit, the Office of the Federal Register note that this order amends EO 8809 (with a see-reference to EO 9323); that is the order's own effect on its parent, not a later event against it. current-law:usc has 1 hit: 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57 note, which prints Ex. Ord. No. 8809 as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 9323, Ex. Ord. No. 10444 (Apr. 10, 1953, 18 F.R. 2069) and Ex. Ord. No. 14085 (section 2, Oct. 3, 2022, 87 F.R. 60541) with no ending statement (release point 119-121, through 2026-10-09). current-law:ecfr has 1 hit that is only a search lead and states no ending. The held text of Executive Order 14085 (87 FR 60541) section 2 amends Executive Order 8809 as amended by 9323 and 10444 by striking men and inserting members and by adding references to the Space Force on or after December 20, 2019 after the August 27, 1940, December 7, 1941 and June 27, 1950 dates; it is recorded as a later event, and under the strike-and-insert ruling the clause continues, amended. The Federal Register issue of April 14, 1953 also prints Army and Air Force regulation notes (32 CFR 578.27 and 878.46, indexed by the packet as an EO 10445 item) whose editorial notes only refer to this order; they are not amendments or an end. The held-corpus search for the number 10444 found no revocation or supersession.
savings_reason: The order has no saving clause. It restates the parent order in full and issues no one-time command, so there is no pending-matter residue; the effect on Executive Order 8809 as amended by 9323 is that the restated paragraph replaces that text. The three bounded searches found no other residue or later instrument besides Executive Order 14085.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end. The restated paragraph states no date, duration or condition ending the medal. The only later instrument found, Executive Order 14085 section 2 (effective 2022-10-03), amends it and keeps it in force; the U.S. Code note still prints it without an ending statement, and the held-corpus search for the number 10444 found no revocation or supersession.
scope_check: One clause covers the whole text (characters 624-2365): the amending instruction and the restated paragraph establishing the Good Conduct Medal, its eligibility rules and its proviso. The order has no numbered sections, so the inventory is a single clause. Executive Order 14085 section 2 changes wording inside the restated paragraph (men to members; Space Force date insertions) within the same clause.
independent_command_check: The restatement of the parent order is completed by the text it sets out; there is no separate one-time command, deadline or revocation, and nothing in the clause is exhausted by performance. The restated eligibility rule is a standing rule that continues with the medal.
savings_check: No saving clause or transitional provision appears in the order. Eligibility dates in the restated paragraph (August 27, 1940; December 7, 1941; June 27, 1950) are standing eligibility criteria, not time limits on the clause. The bounded searches found no preserved right or pending matter needing separate treatment.
